reference_items.native_verdict: Frame data and determinism are still excellent; the resolver is not

checks.observed: damage_health magnitude 20 (declared output 40) against one stationary body: CANTRIP touch 4 applications / 176 damage, LIGHT touch 5 / 220, HEAVY touch 7 / 308, against 1 application / 44 damage at target and at projectile in the same arena. _spawnContact sets ticksEveryF:1 over the class's whole active window and the volume loop at system.js:843 has no per-target dedupe, so the number of times a touch spell lands IS the class's active-frame count. focusBase() charges range_mult 0.85 for touch against 1.00 for target: the cheapest range in the table is also the strongest by 5-8x.

quoteSpell for bind_greater magnitude 90 / 60 s returns focus_cost 111, refused:false. focus_max is 124 on a fresh arena and 88 after 120 f@60 of stepping (the character sheet reclaims H.setWillpower). The cast then emits an EMPTY magic event stream: no cast_start, no focus_spend, no refusal, no input_dropped event, no prose. A body goes down at magnitude 40/50/60/65/70/72 and nothing at all at 74, 76, 78, 80 and 90.
8 identical casts of fire_damage magnitude 40: one distinct damage value (80), 0 determinism violations on every run, guards throwing rather than counting.
same cast under time-of-day 0, time-of-day 13, wall clock +8 h, disposition 100, bounty 5000, weather storm and PRNG seed 9: damage is exactly 80 in all eight arms.

carried from crit-w1-14-r3-9f2c and independently reproduced from the other side: against a STATIONARY body all five damage effects connect at target range (damage_health 44, fire_damage 40, frost_damage 38, shock_damage 40, poison_damage 27 at magnitude 20). In part A, where both bodies were aggroed and therefore moving, fire_damage came back NOT_DELIVERED while damage_health delivered in the same arena. Unrepaired by this round.

reference_items.why_not_ten: The frame data, the commitment model and the determinism are as good as they have been and would carry a 7 alone. Three things stop it: a touch spell that delivers 4-7x its declared output at the cheapest range multiplier in the table; a commissioned, quoted-as-castable spell that produces no event and no message when the button is pressed; and the superseded verdict's unrepaired resolver gap against a moving body.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Dedupe the contact volume per target; emit a refusal event (with focus_cost and focus_max) when the input gate drops a cast for the reservoir; fix the acquisition/lead so a bolt connects with a body moving at walking pace.

reference_items.native_verdict: Three dials, two of them read for the first time this round, and one of the fixes leaks into the archetype

checks.observed: four bodies at 0.3, 2.6, 5.0 and 7.4 m from the volume's own centre (a flat 9.0 m in front of the caster for a resolved_world_point placement). fire_damage r=2 reaches 1 of 4 and r=8 reaches 4 of 4 (312 -> 140 each); frost_damage 1 vs 4 (312 -> 199); poison_damage 1 at r=2 and 3 at r=6, the 7.4 m body untouched at the effect's own 6 m cap. Reader: _geometryFor radius_m = max(area,1) into _spawnVolume v.r and the enclosure test at system.js:846.

bind_lesser magnitude 1 -> power 0.25, hp_max 65; magnitude 90 -> power 4, hp_max 1040. bind_greater 1 -> 0.25/160; 45 -> 2.498/1599. Teardown (__breakBindMagnitude) returns power 1 and hp_max 260/640 at BOTH magnitudes, byte-identical between arms, matching the pre-fix number the builder measured on an independent scratch copy. Inert fix ruled out; control demonstrated live.

magnitude 1 -> the body ends 6.02 m from the caster against a declared leash of 6; magnitude 34 -> 45.01 m against a declared 45. With __breakFleeMotion: 2.38 m at BOTH magnitudes, and calm_beast in the same arena also ends at 2.38 m to the centimetre. The builder's 4.04 m 'coincidence' is the collision's definition, not a shared constant: neither effect writes a position, so both bodies stop where the AI had them on the cast frame, and the number is whatever that arena's frame produces.

SIX identical casts of one commissioned bind_lesser at magnitude 40 (power 2.22 every time, Focus topped up so none is refused) produce summon attack_rating 191, 424, 941, 2089, 4638, 10296 — 86 (drowned_lesser.json's own weapon.attack_rating) multiplied by 2.22 six times. Five casts at magnitude 1 run it the other way: 22, 22, 6, 6, 2, and 86 never returns. hp_max is constant at 577 because hpMax is rebuilt from stat.hp on each spawn — and hp_max is the one field the builder's own AR-1 arm checked. Cause: combat/enemy.js:47 sets `_weapon: weapon` where weapon is stat.weapon (system.js:249), NOT a copy; bindHandler's in-place `body.moves._weapon.attack_rating *= power` therefore writes the statblock. The code comment above that line asserts it is a per-body copy, which is true only of the player's roster path in combat/moves.js.

fire_damage magnitude 20 at duration 0 s, 5 s and 30 s, one stationary body, hp sampled every 20 f@60 for 600 f@60: 1 application, 40 damage, 412 -> 372 flat, and the three hp curves are byte-identical. total(30)/total(0) = 1.00. Morrowind's reading of the 30 s row would be 1080. restore_health at 0 s and 30 s likewise moves nothing. applyEffects sets remaining_f = round(duration_s*60) and step() only decrements it and calls _undo at zero: the row is a lease on a mutation, correct for feather and wrong for a damage-over-time effect. focusBase() charges 0.7*D^0.95 + 0.55*M^0.80*D^0.45 for it.

the builder's finding is withdrawn. Caster wounded to 80/300; absorb_health magnitude 60 at touch takes the target 412 -> 77 and the caster 80 -> 300 (capped). damage_health and drain_health both move the caster 0. The builder measured at magnitude 1, where the transfer is 1 hp. The census collision with damage_health is real; the diagnosis is not.

reference_items.why_not_ten: Two of the three dials were read for the first time this round and both readings survive an independent instrument, which is real progress. Against that: duration is unread on the four effects Morrowind's 'N points for M seconds' is actually about, and the summon fix introduced a permanent, cumulative mutation of a shared statblock that makes the same spell do a different thing every time it is cast.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Copy the weapon block in combat/enemy.js; make a duration on a damage/heal effect tick per second; then re-run the dial census with a world-side-only signature.
reference_items.native_score_note: min-over-axes over RI-MAG02'S OWN eight axes: catalogue size, out-of-fight breadth, formula, determinism, levitation, teleport, the §H rulings, economy. NEITHER failing check maps 1:1 onto one of them, which is why the min is 5 and not 0. `summon-fix-mutates-the-shared-archetype` is a defect in ONE handler writing through a shared object owned by combat/enemy.js; the nearest axis is `determinism`, and that axis's own 0 condition is 'any magnitude range, resist roll or failure chance' — this is none of those, it is deterministic state leakage, so it does not trip the axis's automatic fail. `duration-is-not-read-on-damage-or-heal` has no axis at all: RI-MAG02 §D prices duration and the item never asserts that a duration on a damage effect ticks. THAT ABSENCE IS ITSELF A CORPUS GAP and it is the reason §8 of the markdown writes the acceptance out in full rather than citing a method that does not exist. The 5 is the honest reading of the eight shipped axes with two real defects that sit between them; a future amendment adding a `dial fidelity` axis would score this row lower and should.

It appears in saveState() under magic.custom_spells.

no list of approved combinations exists anywhere in the build; the four declared gates are the only refusals. The declared clamps behave: damage_health at magnitude 999 / duration 40 s / area 9 m is MADE and silently corrected to magnitude 200 / duration 0 / area 0, because that effect's own row forbids the other two.

makeSpell has exactly one caller in the entire build and it is window.__HARNESS; so does enchantQuote. The eight openable menus are inventory, journal, book, levelup, sheet, spells, container, map — `spells` is a list of what is attuned. No NPC in game/data/npcs/** offers a spellmaking or enchanting service; the service vocabulary in the shipped data has 17 values and neither word is among them; no dialogue topic mentions either. enchanting.json names seven enchanters/spellwrights with settlements attached and its own note says 'Four in the world, and walking to one is part of the cost (RI-MAG03 §A, S7)'. None of the seven exists as a person anywhere in the world; their ids appear in exactly one other file, enchant-services.json, as a foreign key to nobody.

reference_items.why_not_ten: The model is Morrowind's and it is good: separate magnitude, duration and area dials, a shared range and class, no whitelist, honest clamps, a real price formula, and it survives a save. It is reachable only from the test harness. Under ARBITRATION §3's CONSUMPTION clause a model whose only consumer is the harness is unmeasurable and therefore 0 from the player's chair; I score 4 rather than 0 because the arithmetic and the gates are demonstrably correct and the missing piece is an access point rather than a system.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Place the seven spellwrights enchanting.json already names, as NPCs in the settlements it already names them at, with a dialogue topic that opens a spellmaking screen driven by quoteSpell.
reference_items.native_score_note: min-over-axes over RI-MAG03's own eight axes: unauthored spells, gate determinism, enchanting arithmetic, the S15 firewall, anti-farm, xul_hesh, the breakage register, economy. `spellmaking-has-no-world-side-surface` maps 1:1 onto NONE of them, because every one of the eight is written as a question about the MODEL and M1's own procedure says 'drive the spellmaking UI through the harness'. Measured strictly against those eight, the axes I could test pass and three were not run. I score 4 rather than 6 because ARBITRATION §5's precedence order puts §3's CONSUMPTION clause ABOVE an item's stated comparison method, and §3 is explicit that a model with no world-side consumer is 0 'exactly as a missing model is'. Applying §3 literally would make this row 0; I score 4 because the arithmetic, the four gates, the clamps and the save round-trip are demonstrably correct and what is missing is an access point rather than a system, and because the item itself invites the harness route — a critic who scored it 6 on M1 as written would be defensible, which is exactly why I have filed the amendment as an arbitration question rather than leaving the next critic to guess.

reference_items.native_verdict: The best instrument this piece has built, with a control that does not reach the thing it controls

checks.observed: --break=nocast makes runOne() skip makeSpell, so base.delivered is false and every one of the 55 rows exits at `if (!base.delivered) { row.verdict='NOT_DELIVERED'; continue; }` BEFORE readDial() is called. '55/55 NOT_DELIVERED, coupled 0, blind 0' is therefore a statement about the delivery gate and says nothing about whether the BLIND/COUPLED comparison can manufacture a coupling — that comparison never ran under the control. Rule 6's second shape: the teardown does not reach the thing under test.

twelve effects cast twice at identical dial settings from the same seed. Six delivered rows: FOUR clean (damage_health, shield, feather, shatter differ in nothing) and TWO not clean — bind_lesser and bind_greater differ at world.summons.json between two identical casts, which is the archetype-mutation defect. Six further rows did not deliver and that is my arena, not the build (see method_deviations).

--break=bindblind and --break=fleeblind are declared in the probe's own USAGE self-test block; reports/w1-14-r3/ contains dials-break-nocast.json and no dials-break-bindblind.json. Run by me: bind_lesser and bind_greater go COUPLED (4 paths) -> BLIND (0 paths) with the reader removed, so the instrument CAN report BLIND on a dial it has just called live. demoralise goes COUPLED (2 paths) -> COUPLED (1 path): __breakFleeMotion disables the flee loop but leaves h_demoralise's writes, so b.fleeLeashM = clamp(magnitude*0.9, 6, 45) is still published through statusReport(). That hook is a PARTIAL teardown and a dial census run under it would still call demoralise's magnitude COUPLED.

the reported '104 declared dials, 26 -> 23' uses 55 magnitude dials; dials.json's own summary declares 48 (magnitude.max > magnitude.min), 37 duration and 12 area = 97. The 7 excluded are cure_paralysis, sap_ward, buoyancy, breathe_water, slowfall, levitate, mark, which the probe itself reports as N/A_FIXED_BY_DATA.

computed from the builder's own dials.json without re-running: every differing path is under world.* (getMagicWorld(), magic's own bookkeeping, which M7 excludes) for 4 magnitude dials (bound_weapon, mend_item, detect_life, detect_key), 7 duration dials (soul_trap, bound_weapon, buoyancy, breathe_water, wall, detect_life, detect_key) and 1 area dial (wall). World-side, dial blindness is 19/48 magnitude, 13/37 duration and 3/12 area = 35 of 97, not 23 of 104. The census v2 computes the M7-strict variant; the dials probe does not.
frenzy_target is written ('e1' on the status readout) and over 1200 f@60 with two bodies 0.7 m apart NEITHER loses a single hp. c.hostileTo has one grep hit in the build and it is the write.

reference_items.why_not_ten: The instrument is a genuine advance — the first thing in the project to turn the duration and area dials at all, with a correct delivery check and a correct INERT classification — and its two headline readings survive an independent re-measurement. It is scored 5 because its control does not exercise its comparator, its own declared self-test was never run, its headline denominator comes from a different population than its numerator, and it counts twelve of magic's own private registers as world-side couplings.

the attunement gate is a rule and not a roll; the S11 buildup meter is integer against an integer threshold; cost.js is pure arithmetic with no PRNG read; volumes re-arm on an integer frame period rather than a per-frame probability. The magnitude dial buys hp, stamina and poise and explicitly not speed — demoralise's flee.speed_mps is a constant with the reason written beside it, which is the right reading of S22.

the attack_rating drift across identical casts (191 -> 10296) is perfectly deterministic and perfectly path-dependent: state leakage, not dice. S26 forbids widening AR-1 to cover an ordinary defect, so it is charged to RI-MAG02 and RI-MAG06 and recorded here only so that nobody mistakes the omission for an oversight.

biggest_gap.what: The spell-making and enchanting systems — the entire Morrowind half of this piece and the reason RI-MAG03 exists — are reachable only from window.__HARNESS. `makeSpell` has exactly one caller in the whole build and it is the test harness; so does `enchantQuote`. The eight menus a player can open are inventory, journal, book, levelup, sheet, spells, container and map, and `spells` is a list of what is already attuned. No NPC in game/data/npcs/** offers a spellmaking or enchanting service; the shipped service vocabulary has 17 values and neither word is among them; no dialogue topic mentions either. game/data/magic/enchanting.json names seven enchanters and spellwrights with settlements attached — journeyman_lilmoth, journeyman_gideon, journeyman_stormhold, journeyman_helstrom, master_blackrose, master_soulrest, recluse_stone_wastes — and its own note reads 'Four in the world, and walking to one is part of the cost (RI-MAG03 §A, S7)'. None of the seven exists as a person anywhere in the world; their ids appear in exactly one other file, enchant-services.json, as a foreign key to nobody.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: ARBITRATION §3's CONSUMPTION clause governs: a model with no demonstrated world-side consumer is unmeasurable and therefore 0, 'exactly as a missing model is — from the player's chair they are the same thing.' RI-MAG03's own bar is blunter: a critic must be able to build, buy and cast a spell that appears nowhere in spells.json, and the moment that matters is walking into the guild and constructing an object that has never existed before. There is nowhere to walk to. Every one of the 97 dials this round spent itself measuring exists so that a player can turn it, and the player has no hands on any of them. Shipped in this state the game has a fixed list of 72 spells — which is precisely the failure the doctrine names: a fixed list of abilities with good frame data is a failure of this piece however well it fights. It is also the cheapest blocking gap on the list, because the arithmetic, the four gates, the clamps, the tier ladder, the commission price, the save round-trip and the refusal prose all exist and all work. What is missing is a person to talk to and a screen to talk on.

remedy.action: Place the seven enchanters/spellwrights enchanting.json already names as NPCs in the settlements it already names them at (lilmoth, gideon, stormhold, helstrom, blackrose, soulrest, and the Stone Wastes recluse), each carrying a `service` of spellmaking or enchanting in game/data/npcs/**. Give each a dialogue topic that opens the commission surface, so the entry point is Morrowind's topic list and not a Souls vendor grid. Add a `spellmaking` mode to ui/system.js's OPENABLE list, driven by quoteSpell — the quote already returns everything the screen needs: focus_base, focus_cost, tier, skill_req, gold, the clamped effect terms and the refusal reason. Do not put one in the starting town: the item's own note makes distance part of the price and S7 backs it.
remedy.acceptance: A probe that NEVER calls H.makeSpell, H.enchantQuote or H.enchanterOpen walks the player to a named settlement, opens a conversation with a named NPC through H.talkTo, selects a spellmaking topic through H.conversationSay, and commissions 19 of 20 tuples that are legal under RI-MAG02 and absent from spells.json — including one three-effect spell, one at an effect's magnitude.max, one at duration.max_s, one whose focus_cost exceeds focus_max, and one deliberately nonsensical (invisibility + area fire_damage) — asserting each appears in saveState(), each computes RI-MAG02 §D's focus_base exactly, and each castable one delivers its commissioned magnitude. The twentieth, the effect-count-over-skill-cap case, is refused with its number. Gold decreases by the quoted price and by nothing else.

secondary_observations.what: THE SUMMON FIX PERMANENTLY MUTATES THE ARCHETYPE IT SCALES. bindHandler writes body.moves._weapon.attack_rating in place; combat/enemy.js:47 sets `_weapon: weapon` where weapon is stat.weapon (system.js:249) and NOT a copy — the copy in combat/moves.js is the PLAYER's roster path, which is what the code comment above the write is describing. Six identical casts of one commissioned bind_lesser at magnitude 40 produce attack_rating 191, 424, 941, 2089, 4638, 10296: 86 (drowned_lesser.json's own weapon.attack_rating) times 2.22, six times. Five casts at magnitude 1 run it down to 22, 22, 6, 6, 2. hp_max is constant, and hp_max is the field the builder's own AR-1 arm checked.

A TOUCH SPELL CASTS ITSELF ONCE PER ACTIVE FRAME. _spawnContact sets ticksEveryF:1 across the class's whole active window and the volume loop has no per-target dedupe. damage_health magnitude 20 (declared output 40): CANTRIP touch 4 applications / 176 damage, LIGHT 5 / 220, HEAVY 7 / 308, against 1 / 44 at target and projectile. focusBase() charges touch the LOWEST range multiplier in the table (0.85). Both the census and the dials probe prefer touch (rangeFor order self, touch, target, projectile, area_at_range), so much of the catalogue has been measured through a 4-7x applicator for three rounds.

THE ROUND'S CONSUMPTION EVIDENCE IS THE SUMMON FIGHTING ITS CASTER. tools/harness/w1-14-r3-summon.mjs calls H.aggro(sid) on its own summon and reports 'damage the player took' — 41 at magnitude 1 against 164 at magnitude 90, control 0 because the room is otherwise empty. engine.spawn(id,x,z,{side:'ally'}) never reads side (engine.js:6213) and CombatSystem.spawnEnemy constructs new CombatBody(id,'E',...). Confirmed from outside: the summon arrives as kind 'enemy' with no side, team, faction or summoned field on the entity or the body. I could not stage a three-body fight to show it refusing to defend and record that as not measured.

DURATION IS NOT READ ON THE FOUR EFFECTS IT MATTERS MOST FOR. fire_damage magnitude 20 at 0 s, 5 s and 30 s produces three byte-identical hp curves — one step of 40, flat for 580 frames. Morrowind's reading of the 30 s row is 1080. Acceptance for round 4 is written out in §8 of the markdown, including the trap that voided my own first attempt (an out-of-combat body regenerates, so the window must be short enough that regeneration cannot answer the question).

A CAST OVER THE RESERVOIR IS A SILENT DROP. quoteSpell returns focus_cost 111 / refused:false for bind_greater at magnitude 90; focus_max is 124 fresh and 88 after 120 f@60 of stepping; the cast then emits an EMPTY event stream. Bodies go down at magnitude 40/50/60/65/70/72 and not at 74 and above. The uncastable band is, arithmetically, the flat part of the scaling law — power saturates at 4.000 and magnitude 72 already returns 3.996 — so the answer to 'is a scaling law you cannot cast a fix' is mostly yes; what is not acceptable is a commissioned spell that produces no event and no message when the button is pressed.

THE BUILDER'S absorb_health FINDING IS WITHDRAWN. With the caster wounded to 80/300, absorb_health at magnitude 60 takes the target 412 -> 77 and the caster 80 -> 300; damage_health and drain_health move the caster 0. The builder measured at magnitude 1, where the transfer is one hit point. The census collision with damage_health is real and the diagnosis attached to it is not.

THE 4.04 m COINCIDENCE IS THE COLLISION'S DEFINITION, NOT A SHARED CONSTANT. With the flee loop disabled, demoralise ends 2.38 m out at magnitude 1 AND at magnitude 34, and calm_beast in the same arena also ends at 2.38 m to the centimetre. Both effects set aggro=false, yielded=true, move=null and write no position; EnemyController's yielded branch writes none either. So both bodies stop wherever the AI had them on the cast frame, and that distance is whatever the arena produces — 4.04 m in the builder's, 2.38 m in mine.

THE TREE DOES NOT BOOT AT HEAD AND IT IS NOT THIS PIECE. 63f41ef throws at Engine._installCanon: game/data/lore/canon.json has 2 unresolved references (CF-D015/A, CF-D018/A — topic info for the actor `notary` removed by a concurrent dialogue piece). No engine can be constructed and every stepping probe in the project is down. Rule 13: a fail-closed assertion is live against data that no longer exists.

method_deviations: MEASURED AGAINST A PINNED EXPORT, NOT THE WORKING TREE. HEAD does not boot (canon register, another piece). git archive 34d1387 game | tar -x, and `git diff 9aeb839 34d1387 -- game/src/sim/magic/ game/data/magic/ game/src/harness/api.js` is empty, so the pin carries the builder's code byte-for-byte.

MY OWN FIRST DURATION RUN WAS VOID AND I ALMOST PUBLISHED IT. Part I reported `applied 1, damage 0` for fire, frost and poison at every duration over a 2100 f@60 window. Part J then measured the same bolts doing 27-44 damage over 300 f@60, and part K's hp curve shows the wound open at 600 f@60 and closed by 2100 — an out-of-combat body regenerates and I had given it 35 seconds. Had I believed the first run I would have published 'three of the five damage effects deal no damage', which is false.

SIX OF MY TWELVE PART-A NULL ROWS DID NOT DELIVER AND THAT IS MY ARENA. I set area_r_m to 4 on every area-capable effect, which turns the geometry into a volume placed a flat 9.0 m in front of the caster while my bodies stood at 1.4 and 5.2 m. The null reading stands on the six rows that delivered.

I COULD NOT STAGE A THREE-BODY FIGHT to show the summon declining to defend its caster. At 2.4 m and at 8 m the hostile RUSHed, hit RI-AI01's leash and returned to its anchor without swinging, in the control arm too. Recorded as not measured rather than as a zero.
AR-2 NOT RE-RUN; RI-MAG04, RI-MAG05, RI-PRG03 and RI-QST05 NOT RE-MEASURED and carried at the superseded verdict's values, excluded from this verdict's min.

CONTENTION. node tools/contention.mjs --gate returned WAIT for the first third of this run (3 browser instances, load 5.07 per core against a 4.0 ceiling). All instrument writing, the whole static analysis in §2 and the whole of §11 were done offline before a browser started. I did not proceed past a WAIT: every run launched after a GO, one browser at a time, never in parallel. Every number published is a frame count, a hit point or an event count and is load-independent; NO TIMING FIGURE IS PUBLISHED, which is why none appears.

arbitration_questions: RI-MAG03's M1 says 'drive the spellmaking UI through the harness', which reads as licence to grade the model. ARBITRATION §3's CONSUMPTION clause says a model whose only consumer is the harness is 0. I have applied §3, because §5's precedence order puts the Arbitration Rule above an item's stated comparison method — but the item should be amended to say so, or a future critic will grade the same system 6 and be defensible.

Is a per-frame re-application of a contact spell (§7) an RI-MAG01 defect or an RI-CMB defect? The volume loop belongs to magic and the dedupe convention belongs to combat. I have charged it to RI-MAG01.

self_audit.escalation: Rung 1 (re-run the builder's probe) would have returned the builder's numbers, and most of them are right. Rung 3 (build an independent instrument) confirmed the area dial and both fixes. What produced this verdict was rung 4, the second-order property: not 'is the dial read' but 'what does the control control' (§2), 'what is the consumption arm consuming' (§6), 'what happens if you cast the same spell twice' (§5), and 'who can reach any of this' (§11).

notes: Two of the three attacks the brief set me failed and the round deserves the credit: the area dial is genuinely read and both fixes are genuinely real with control arms that go red. The instrument that found them is the best this piece has produced. It is scored where it is because the round's own control does not exercise its comparator, its declared self-test was never run, its headline fix leaks into a shared statblock, and the system the whole piece exists to make possible has no door.
